answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can come from requiring each new identity to stake a non-refundable deposit of rare digital assets extracted from simulated shale deposits, then prove continuous participation by maintaining a living trellis of verified interaction graphs that only yield nectar rewards after multi-epoch peer validation. Attackers face escalating computational and capital costs to forge such enduring structures, making mass identity creation prohibitively expensive compared to honest long-term contribution.
